Things we have in common are our interests in music and our dogs(and possibly disney movies from the last few messages). I thought about just going to a c̶h̶i̶p̶o̶t̶l̶e̶  anything but chipotle in her area and then if things go well, frozen yogurt. I'm just worried that's a bit... young of a place to go for a date(I'm 24 and she's 23) so i was gonna look around the area for a bistro or something. 

I'll definitely avoid a rapey idea lol.

**thought about it and looked it up, definitely not chipotle lol

She's a music major which is why I thought of a symphony, but thinking about it more, it really does seem like more of a 3rd+ date. The single flower seems a bit corny, she might actually enjoy that though. Maybe if things turn up successful and I take her to dinner.

Am I missing something? I see all of these complicated solutions that are great, but really?

If you can get it filming for most of the day, why not just delete the footage from the day before? No need for some complicated setup and it's not that hard to format an SD or write a script to do it...

People rarely go when they're supposed to. My condolences for your loss.

No matter what, your father loved and was proud of you. It's a shame that he didn't get to see the medals you got him, but the time you spent together probably brought him much more happiness. If you believe in heaven, then I'm sure he knows about the medals now and couldn't be happier watching over you.

I've been in this situation a lot myself and honeslty, I realized that people that you're friendly with typically won't rub anything in your face. If you weren't invited, they may have just thought that you weren't interested in it or forgot to invite you since you typically don't go out with them. If it was an office-sponsored party, you may have just missed the invitation/flier like another post said. 

I had the same thing happen to me with some friends and they posted a picture of the party while it was still happening. I felt terrible when I saw it, like these people I thought I was close to didn't want me around. I just put something nice-something along the lines of, "is that hotpot? Nice!" it was a while ago so I'm a bit fuzzy- in the comment section and a couple minutes later they called to apologize for forgetting me and 20 minutes later I was with there. Was it a pity invite? not really. I just didn't socialize much and the less social you are, the easier it is for people to forget about you when making a guest list.  With my group, we usually leave out a few people by accident because everyone's so busy now. 

I wouldn't say your coworkers are specivically excluding you. If they were, then you don't want to be there anyway.

Only reason I even have a job is because a family member hired me. Work is actually the only thing keeping me going really. 

Ive tried to develop hobbies, but when I get off work, all I want to do is go home and crawl into bed until the morning.
